notes: What the PWA and the desktop shell may differ on, declared once. scripts/tauri_parity.py refuses a route in app/src/App.tsx without an entry here, and a read of isTauri / isDesktopShell / window.__TAURI__ in app/src that is not counted here. shell-parity.spec.ts compares the routes below in both platforms and removes only the selectors listed under platform_only.

platform_branches.desktop: the dialog runs the signed Tauri updater and reports download progress

platform_branches.surface: chat header: window controls, the traffic-light clearance, and the backend version message
platform_branches.web: no controls, no left inset and no version message: the browser draws the window chrome and has no shell to ask
platform_branches.desktop: minimize and maximize at the header's right edge, an extra left inset when the sidebar is a rail so the first control clears the overlaid traffic lights, and one read of the shell's backend-parity verdict at boot

platform_branches.surface: window controls, passed through to the chat view model
platform_branches.web: false, from useTauriWindow
platform_branches.desktop: true, from useTauriWindow

platform_branches.web: the browser file picker
platform_branches.desktop: the shell's native open dialog (pickOpenPath)

platform_branches.desktop: pick_folder through the shell, then the same /api/import

platform_branches.surface: screen lock while a turn streams
platform_branches.web: the Screen Wake Lock API, when the browser has it
platform_branches.desktop: set_keep_awake through the shell

platform_branches.web: no bridge, so no listeners are installed

platform_branches.web: false; windowVisible stays true
platform_branches.desktop: true while the shell's event API is present

platform_branches.web: absent; invoke logs and resolves without a shell
platform_branches.desktop: minimize_window, maximize_window, close_window, show_window, hide_window

platform_branches.desktop: http://127.0.0.1:8765 unless VITE_API_URL overrides it

platform_branches.desktop: true

platform_branches.desktop: shown: the shortcuts area owns one saveable global opt-in

platform_branches.surface: the backend version the shell started
platform_branches.web: no command channel, so nothing is claimed and no message appears

platform_only.reason: The shell draws its own title bar; a browser tab already has minimize and maximize. Both items sit in the header menu and exist only in the shell's DOM while that menu is open.

The PWA registers /service-worker.js for offline and update; the shell is installed and updated by the Tauri updater. Both parity contexts block service workers, because a worker answers /api from its own fetch context below page.route; the web-only registration is proven in its own test.
